summary: Heterogeneous stream mix triggered gradual throughput sag and transient GPU shortages in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Glyph Labs reported a gradual rise in p99 latency and an observable drop in sustained throughput in their Dedicated GPU pool during their midday traffic window (11:30–13:10 PDT) on 2026-03-13. The degradation started subtly and progressed over ~75 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer reported increased API timeouts and some 5xx errors for streaming endpoints used by their realtime assistant.
- Throughput dropped ~18% p50 and ~35% p99 for affected routes.
- No full outages; requests queued and some fell back to slower model variant causing quality regressions.

Timeline (high level):
- 11:28 PDT: Glyph Labs traffic spike begins (short-lived fanout streams + several long-lived background streams).
- 11:31 PDT: Monitoring alerted on autoscale decisions (scale up delayed).
- 12:00 PDT: p99 latency trending up; SLO breaches approaching.
- 12:45 PDT: Support contacted; ticket opened.
- 13:10 PDT: Temporary mitigation applied (rate-limit on noisy tenant, adjust autoscaler window).

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) for Glyph Labs
- Region: us-west-2
- Models: gpt-4o-redwood-v1 (primary), fallback: llama-2-70b
- Runtime: serving-runtime v3.14.2, autoscaler v1.9.0

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1. Deploy mixed workload: 60% short (<1s) high-concurrency streaming calls, 40% long-lived (>30s) low-CPU streams pinned to KV-cache.
2. Keep sustained concurrency matching Glyph Labs midday profile (approx 2.5k concurrent streams across pool).
3. Observe autoscaler decisions and batcher behavior over 60–90 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Gradual throughput sag (p99 and p50 degradation) without immediate scheduler errors.
- Autoscaler took repeated small steps instead of a single efficient scale; scale decisions lagged behind effective load shift.
- GPU attachments showed transient shortages: short-lived allocation rejections for new batches, increased queueing time in the batcher.
- Prefetch/KV-cache growth on long streams caused slot occupancy to appear higher than compute demand alone predicted.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler to detect the sustained increased demand and provision capacity within configured SLO window.
- Batcher to maintain throughput without serializing small streams into long stream slots.

Initial hypothesis:
- Mixed workload (very short ephemeral streams + many long-lived context-heavy streams) caused slot misrepresentation: autoscaler and scheduler saw high slot utilization but lower effective compute throughput, leading to underscaling and slow incremental autoscale steps. Noisy tenant pattern amplified GPU attachment churn and triggered fallback routing.

Attachments/links:
- Grafana dashboard snapshots: link omitted for customer privacy
- Related runbook: confluence.company.com/display/OPS/Dedicated+Pool+Noisy+Tenant+Runbook
investigation_notes: 11:40 PDT: batcher logs show repeated small-batch serialization: worker-ids 73f1.. -> lock contends at 11:38–11:52.
11:55 PDT: autoscaler emitted 5 scale-up decisions but each adjusted by 1-2 slots; policy min_reconcile_interval respected causing slow ramp (policy configured: step=+1, window=60s).
12:05 PDT: scheduler reports transient allocation failures (code ALLOC_REJECT) for 27 requests/min; trace IDs: [trace-a1b2, trace-c3d4].
12:20 PDT: KV-cache growth on long streams reached 78% of per-GPU cache quota for several GPUs leading to fragmentation and preemptive eviction activity.
12:35 PDT: top-talkers list: one internal background job from Glyph Labs (job-id gglyph-backfill) holding long-lived streams; correlation with p99 rise is high (Pearson r=0.71).
12:50 PDT: observed fallback routing executing to llama-2-70b for ~6% of requests due to capacity signaling, causing customer-facing quality drop.

Mitigation applied 13:10 PDT: throttled noisy background job via temporary tenant-level rate limit; autoscaler window reduced from 60s to 30s for the pool as emergency change. Immediate improvement: p99 dropped ~22% within 10 minutes.

next_steps: Follow-up with Glyph Labs to reschedule long-running background jobs to off-peak windows; recommend use of Dedicated burst slots for heavy prefetch jobs.
Engineering action: update autoscaler policy options to add mixed-workload detection heuristics (detect high KV-cache occupancy + low compute throughput) before step-scaling; ticket INT-4129 created.
Investigate making a heuristic that counts long-lived KV-cache pinned streams separately when computing desired capacity.
Create a short runbook entry for Support/SRE for identifying mixed short/long stream incidents and emergency mitigations (tenant throttles, autoscaler window adjustments).
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: noisy background job throttled and autoscaler reconcile window temporarily reduced. Partial recovery observed (p99 improved ~22% within 10 minutes). Awaiting engineering changes for a permanent fix. Post-incident meeting scheduled with customer for 2026-03-15.
